quote: Yes. I already have solar. You already have solar?
stewart_read: This is the orphaned_flow trigger point — customer confirms existing solar system. The rep correctly pivots into ownership/loan-vs-lease/panel-company questions right after, which is the schema-correct start of the orphaned flow.
coaching_implication: Confirm the rep recognizes this as the orphaned-flow trigger and is trained to run the full required question set from here, not just the ownership piece.

quote: We just need to see your Who are you? Who what company are you?
stewart_read: The customer has to stop the verify flow to ask who's calling — the rep's opening at 00:03 ('Hey. This is Randy.') never stated the company, so legitimacy wasn't established until the customer forced it a minute in.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep simply forgot the company name in the opener. Strategic read doesn't hold here — there's no indication the delay was intentional; it reads as an omission the customer had to correct.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always state company name in the first line, even on inbound/callback-style contacts, per protocols.how_did_you_get_my_number's honest_specificity principle.

stewart_read: Rep gets the panel company but the orphaned_flow schema also requires panel size in watts and whether the system is currently working — neither was asked. The 'is your system working' question is a hard_dq trigger if answered negatively, so skipping it leaves a qualification gap.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may have judged the battery-add conversation didn't need full requalification since a specialist would cover it. But the schema marks these as required orphaned_flow items, and 'working system' is explicitly hard_dq-relevant, so the omission is a real gap, not a deliberate defer.
coaching_implication: Drill the full orphaned_flow question set (own/lease, company, panel size in watts, system working) as a fixed sequence whenever existing solar is confirmed — don't stop after ownership and company.

quote: I don't remember who it was. I thought I talked to somebody. But I have some additional questions
stewart_read: Customer flags he has 'additional questions' left over from a prior contact, but the rep never asks what those questions are — that content would be immediately useful for the specialist's callback and for the handoff brief.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep let a content-gathering opportunity go because he was focused on scheduling logistics, not because it was strategically deferred — nothing in the transcript shows an intent to circle back to it.
coaching_implication: When a customer says they have lingering questions, capture even a one-line summary before transferring — it's free intel for the closer and shows the customer their concern was heard.

quote: He can actually give you a call here within the next, hour or two.
stewart_read: The call ends on a window ('hour or two', later narrowed to 'four and five') rather than a locked time, and there's no explicit 'is that fair?' handshake — the close is procedurally soft even though the customer verbally agrees.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep is working with what the specialist actually gave him (an availability window, not a fixed slot), so the softness may be inherited from the specialist's own vagueness rather than the rep's failure to anchor.
coaching_implication: Even when the specialist only gives a window, the rep should convert it into the tightest possible commitment ('he'll call you at 4:30 sharp') and get an explicit yes/fair confirmation before hanging up.

stewart_read: This is the closest the rep gets to a handshake question, but it's asked about a two-hour window, not a specific time, and the customer's reply ('I'll try... I gotta make sure I hear him when he calls') signals real uncertainty the rep doesn't fully resolve beyond offering a heads-up text.
coaching_implication: Treat 'I'll try' as a live signal the appointment is fragile — worth a firmer confirmation loop, not just a text-before-call mitigation.

quote: I can have him, like, shoot you a text message before just to make sure you're, ready for that call.
stewart_read: Rep substitutes a text-heads-up for a hard-locked time slot, directly addressing the customer's stated worry about being at the plant and missing the call — a reasonable trust-building compromise given the customer's real constraint.
coaching_implication: Good instinct to solve the stated logistics problem (being at work) — pair this with a tighter time anchor next time so the fix addresses both the access problem and the vagueness problem.
